summary: Green Island light at the entrance to Blue Hill Bay, Maine: built 1856-57, a fog bell in 1900, discontinued in the 1930s and now a private island property.

structures.note: White cylindrical tower with attached one-and-a-half story dwelling (LighthouseFriends). Discontinued in 1933 or 1934.
Replacement skeletal tower; toppled in 2016 and replaced by a light on a post.

access.note: Privately owned. Grounds, dwelling and tower closed; best viewed from the water or the air (LighthouseFriends).

visit.note: Walking out at low tide is not advised (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Federal government bought Green Island from Abraham Flye for $150.
USLHS gives 1857 for the tower; LighthouseFriends gives 1856 for construction.
Fourth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends); USLHS gives 1857 for the original lens.
Fifth-order Henry-Lepaute lens in the lantern by 1863.
Significant work on the dwelling and boathouse.
Fog bell struck by machinery, 15 September 1900.
Keeper Chandler helped free a vessel that ran aground near the light on 11 October 1928.
Old light replaced by an automated light on a skeletal tower at deactivation (LighthouseFriends, 1 May 1934).
Bought by a private owner for use as a residence.
Skeletal tower toppled; Coast Guard replaced the light with one shown from a post.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The station record asks whether the light is still lit. The historic 1857 light was discontinued. LighthouseFriends describes a flashing green light on the island that replaced it, first on a skeletal tower and, after 2016, on a post. The 'lit' status refers to the replacement aid.

notes_for_editor: Few primary sources were available for this station. Only the 1900 fog-bell line and the 1928 bulletin index entry are from official reports, and the 1856/1857 construction dates and the 1933/1934 discontinuance date are unresolved between USLHS and LighthouseFriends. The USCG Historian's Blue Hill Bay Light page (archived copy) returned a 403 when read through fetch_text, so it is not cited. Other station-record claims (automated 1935, Wikipedia's 1935 skeletal tower) are not verified here. Private owners named in LighthouseFriends are not named in the story. The station record calls the tower 'brick'; LighthouseFriends does not say, so the story says 'white cylindrical tower' and the material is not asserted. Shape: six chapters, each with sourced material, at moderate length (the guide's moderate shape is 2-4 chapters). The editor may collapse the shape to fewer chapters. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the LighthouseFriends sentence about the 1928 report is garbled in the cached text ('Chandler had to the matter to the sheriff'), so the story says only that the matter went to the sheriff. The earlier story text said the bay was named for Green Island, which reversed LighthouseFriends (the light station is named for the bay); the story now says that. The 1856/1857 and 1933/1934 disagreements are stated in the text.
